Subject: Subprocessor disclosure for BlueLedger onboarding

Hi Jasmine / Kimberly,

As we're moving into the integration and Data Processing Agreement (DPA) execution, our security and legal teams have a couple of clarifying asks about your subprocessors. Please see the items below — can you confirm by EOD Monday if possible?

1) Current subprocessor roster and which subprocessors will be in the request path for BlueLedger production traffic.
2) For any caching/edge partners, do they persist request bodies or logs that may contain account identifiers? If so, retention and residency details.
3) SOC 2 / security attestation for any processors that handle customer-derived telemetry or logs.
4) If new subprocessors are temporary (pilot/onboarding), please include expected duration and fallback plan.

We will need this to attach to the DPA addendum and procurement checklist. Attaching the vendor inventory template for convenience.

Thanks,
Elena

Hi Elena — thanks for the clear list. Quick ack: we'll get you an inventory and concise answers today. High level up front: most of our core processors are listed in the attached roster; there is a short-term caching partner being used for burst traffic in the EU region (EdgePulse) that was engaged as a temporary pilot.

Attachments included: redwood_subprocessor_roster_v3.xlsx (full inventory).

Short answers:
- Persistence: EdgePulse is configured as a transient edge cache. It stores encrypted cache entries and does not retain full request payloads by default; retention for keys is 24 hours unless an incident requires extended logging (rare).
- Scope: EdgePulse handles HTTP-level caching (response fragments) and telemetry for edge performance only — we do not send customer message bodies to them for indexing.
- Evidence: SOC 2 snapshot and a short evidence summary for EdgePulse will follow within 24 hours (we're collecting the vendor's attestations).
- Duration: pilot window is 90 days with automatic rollback to our on-prem pool if performance or compliance items surface.

I'll follow up with the SOC 2 excerpts and a short evidence PDF. Kimberly — can you confirm whether we need a DPA addendum signature for this temporary partner or if the existing DPA covers it (procurement asked)?

Best,
Jasmine Liu
Director, Privacy & Trust Operations
Redwood Inference

Hi Jasmine / Kimberly,

Couple quick procurement/security clarifications before we move to signature:
- Can you confirm whether EdgePulse receives any identifiers that would allow re-identification (customer IDs, tenant IDs, user IDs) in either request URIs, headers, or cache keys?
- If there is any ephemeral keying that references account IDs, please provide the exact format and confirm whether those keys are reversible.
- For the SOC 2 / attestations, we will need the vendor's report redacted and a short one-page summary that maps the control areas relevant to log handling (retention, encryption at rest & transit, access control).
- Finally, please confirm the contingency plan: if EdgePulse is disabled, how will traffic be routed and what is the expected RTO?

Procurement is aiming to finalize the DPA addendum this week; the answers above will determine whether we require an explicit subprocessor approval appendix.

Regards,
BlueLedger Procurement Team
procurement@blueledger.com

From: Jasmine Liu <jasmine_liu@redwood.ai>

On Sat, Nov 21, 2026 at 08:03 AM +0000 procurement@blueledger.com wrote:
> Can you confirm whether EdgePulse receives any identifiers that would allow re-identification (customer IDs, tenant IDs, user IDs) in either request URIs, headers, or cache keys?
>
> If there is any ephemeral keying that references account IDs, please provide the exact format and confirm whether those keys are reversible.

Hi — thanks for the follow-up. Answers below (concise):

1) Identifiers: EdgePulse receives only opaque cache keys. Cache keys are hashed values derived from the request path + a nonce; we do not include tenant IDs or raw user identifiers in the key construction. Example key pattern: sha256(path || nonce || salt). Keys are non-reversible without the salt, which is stored in our KMS.

2) Request bodies: We do NOT send full request bodies to EdgePulse. Only response fragments relevant to caching are sent; sensitive payloads are explicitly excluded in the routing rules.

3) Retention & encryption: Default retention is 24 hours for cache entries; in the event of a support incident we may extend retention up to 7 days with documented approval and audit log entries. All cached objects are encrypted at rest using customer-isolated keys (KMS). Transit uses TLS 1.3.

4) Evidence: Attached is a short vendor evidence summary for EdgePulse (edgepulse_evidence_summary.pdf). We are also providing the vendor's SOC 2 Type II cover page and control mapping in the Drive folder here: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2b3c-example-dataflow

5) Contingency / RTO: If EdgePulse is disabled, traffic routes to our Dedicated onshore pool (EU region) with a failover path automated via our routing policy. Expected RTO is under 3 minutes for routing convergence; cold cache effect may add up to 60s of additional latency for warmed segments. We will include these failover details in the addendum.

6) Contracting note: Kimberly — we recommend a brief DPA addendum that references the temporary pilot and includes the 90-day window + rollback trigger language. Procurement — if you prefer an explicit approvals appendix we can produce that; otherwise the addendum will suffice.

Let me know if you'd like a short 30-min call to walk through the controls; happy to set one up next week.

Best,
Jasmine Liu
Director, Privacy & Trust Operations
Redwood Inference
